item.title: Fiji Bulikula go down fighting against Jillaroos in historic World Cup semi-final
item.description: The Vodafone Fiji Bulikula have gone down fighting 30-14 against world champions Australia in their first Rugby League World Cup semi-final. The Bulikula were outscored six tries to two, with Australian winger Abbi Church scoring four tries.
item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Fiji Bulikula have gone down fighting 30-14 against world champions Australia in their first Rugby League World Cup semi-final.

The Bulikula were outscored six tries to two, with Australian winger Abbi Church scoring four tries.

Maria Paseka and Luisa Yaranamua scored tries for the Bulikula.

Fiji put the Jillaroos under pressure in the first half, holding them scoreless until the 22nd minute.

The two teams were locked at 8-8 at half-time.

Bulikula captain Sereana Naitokatoka says it was an amazing game, and she is proud of all her 'lewas' for putting in the hard work from the first minute until the final whistle.

Naitokatoka also acknowledges the fans watching back home in Fiji, especially those from her village of Naisomua in Naitasiri.

She says the Bulikula are warriors and promises to see everyone at the next World Cup.

Meanwhile, Jillaroos captain Isabelle Kelly says it is incredible to see what the Bulikula have achieved by reaching the semi-final.

Kelly says their achievement means a lot for young girls watching in Fiji, as the team continues to pave the way for the next generation.g girls watching in Fiji, and paving the way for them.

item.title: Bulileka resident with special needs struggles with unreliable water supply
item.description: A resident of Low-Cost Bulileka is appealing to the Water Authority of Fiji to urgently address ongoing water supply problems, saying the situation is particularly challenging for him and his sister, who both have special needs. While speaking to fijvillage News Freddie Lal says he is struggling to secure enough water for their household.
item.content:encoded:
A resident of Low-Cost Bulileka is appealing to the Water Authority of Fiji to urgently address ongoing water supply problems, saying the situation is particularly challenging for him and his sister, who both have special needs.

While speaking to fijvillage News Freddie Lal says he is struggling to secure enough water for their household.

Lal says the water supply has been unreliable for quite some time, with water often reaching their area late at night.

He says his physical condition makes it difficult for him to stay awake late at night to collect and store water when supply is available.

Lal says the little water remaining in their drum will only last until today, leaving them worried about how they will manage tomorrow.

He also says his attempts to contact the Water Authority have been unsuccessful, as phone lines are often engaged or calls go unanswered.

Lal says other residents of Low-Cost Bulileka have also been experiencing water supply problems for a long time.

He is appealing to the Government and relevant authorities to urgently look into the issue and ensure affected households have a reliable water supply.

item.title: Kamikamica stresses unity, respect and understanding this Diwali
item.description: Respectful dialogue, consideration of different perspectives and a commitment to every Fijian's dignity are essential as Fiji continues its constitutional review. This is the message from Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce and Business Development Manoa Kamikamica in his Diwali message.
item.content:encoded:
Respectful dialogue, consideration of different perspectives and a commitment to every Fijian's dignity are essential as Fiji continues its constitutional review.

This is the message from Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce and Business Development Manoa Kamikamica in his Diwali message.

Kamikamica says this year's theme, "One Fiji, One Light: Building Understanding, Respect and Unity", reminds Fijians that despite their different faiths and traditions, they share common hopes for peace, opportunity and a better future.

He says Diwali's message of understanding and goodwill is particularly important as the country continues its constitutional review.

Kamikamica says these values also reflect Fiji's economic aspirations, stressing that prosperity must mean more than material wealth and should create secure livelihoods, dignified work and opportunities for families to progress.

He says the Government continues to strengthen entrepreneurship and economic participation through business support, co-operative development and training, particularly in rural and maritime communities.

Kamikamica says Diwali celebrates the triumph of righteousness over evil, knowledge over ignorance and light over darkness.

He also highlights the significance of the return of Lord Rama, Sita and Lakshmana to Ayodhya, while the blessings associated with Goddess Lakshmi, Lord Ganesha and Goddess Saraswati represent prosperity, wisdom, knowledge and new beginnings.

On behalf of his family and the Ministry, Kamikamica extends Diwali greetings to Hindu families in Fiji and abroad, and hopes the festival brings peace and happiness while inspiring all Fijians to treat one another with kindness and respect.

item.title: Singh family celebrates Diwali with prayers, sweets and family gatherings
item.description: Diwali festival serves as a reminder of the victory of good over evil, light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance. This was revealed by Shagrika Shayal Singh of Nawaicoba, Nadi, saying Diwali commemorates the return of Lord Rama, Mata Sita and Lakshman to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile, following Lord Rama's victory over Ravana.
item.content:encoded:
Diwali festival serves as a reminder of the victory of good over evil, light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance.

This was revealed by Shagrika Shayal Singh of Nawaicoba, Nadi, saying Diwali commemorates the return of Lord Rama, Mata Sita and Lakshman to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile, following Lord Rama's victory over Ravana.

She says she celebrated Diwali by visiting the temple with her husband before visiting her parents' home, where friends also came over to share sweets and spend time together.

Singh who is celebrating her first Diwali with her in laws says she helped her mother-in-law prepare sweets for the celebrations, with the two staying up until 11pm despite her work commitments.

She says the celebrations also included sharing snacks, catching up with friends, taking photographs and making TikTok videos.

Singh says the family also planned to offer prayers, light diyas and set off firecrackers, which are her husband's favourite part of the celebrations.

However, she is urging Fijians to be considerate when setting off firecrackers, particularly around young children and household pets who may be frightened by the loud noises.

Singh says she personally dislikes firecrackers because her dog gets frightened by them.

She is wishing all Fijians a happy Diwali and encouraging everyone to celebrate safely while being mindful of others.

item.title: Protecting Fiji's children from drugs is everyone's responsibility – Tikoduadua
item.description: Minister for Defence and Veterans Affairs Pio Tikoduadua is urging families and communities to take an active role in protecting young people from illicit drugs, warning that the future of Fiji's children is at stake. Speaking at the launch of the 2026 Vodafone Ratu Sukuna Bowl at Albert Park in Suva on Saturday, Tikoduadua says drug abuse is damaging families, harming communities and taking away
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Defence and Veterans Affairs Pio Tikoduadua is urging families and communities to take an active role in protecting young people from illicit drugs, warning that the future of Fiji's children is at stake.

Speaking at the launch of the 2026 Vodafone Ratu Sukuna Bowl at Albert Park in Suva on Saturday, Tikoduadua says drug abuse is damaging families, harming communities and taking away opportunities from young people.

He says the fight against drugs is everyone's responsibility and cannot be left to Police and other authorities alone.

As part of this year's Ratu Sukuna Bowl campaign, members of the Republic of Fiji Military Forces and Fiji Police Force will visit schools and communities in Nadi, Lautoka and Labasa on November 12 and 14 to raise awareness about the dangers of illicit drugs.

Government representatives will also participate in the awareness programmes.

This year's competition carries the theme "Drug-Free Fiji" and the slogan "One Goal, Our Mission".

Tikoduadua says the Ratu Sukuna Bowl is more than a sporting competition between the RFMF and Fiji Police Force, as it also provides an opportunity to promote drug awareness and encourage communities to protect young people.

He says that, as a father whose children serve in both the military and Police, he understands the concerns families have about drug-related crime and the safety of their loved ones.

The Minister stresses that drug abuse can damage physical and mental health, contribute to crime and place additional pressure on families and communities.

Tikoduadua is calling on every Fijian to reject illicit drugs, make responsible choices and work together to protect the next generation.

item.title: Fuel costs rise by nearly $300M for Fiji Airways, another loss expected - Scurrah
item.description: Fiji Airways is expected to record another financial loss in 2026 as the airline faces nearly $300 million in additional fuel costs due to the volatility in fuel prices compared to last year. CEO and Managing Director Paul Scurrah revealed this during fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan, saying the airline continues to face significant financial challenges, with fuel prices having more th
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Airways is expected to record another financial loss in 2026 as the airline faces nearly $300 million in additional fuel costs due to the volatility in fuel prices compared to last year.

CEO and Managing Director Paul Scurrah revealed this during fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan, saying the airline continues to face significant financial challenges, with fuel prices having more than doubled compared to 2025.

Scurrah says although Fiji Airways has not finalised its financial results for 2026, he would not be surprised if the airline records another loss.

He says rising fuel prices are affecting airlines around the world, forcing Fiji Airways to review its spending and make difficult decisions to remain financially sustainable.

Scurrah says the airline also continues to carry significant debt and accumulated losses from the COVID-19 pandemic, making the current fuel crisis even more challenging.

He says Fiji Airways could have cut flights and grounded aircraft to reduce its losses, but such a decision would have had serious consequences for Fiji's tourism industry and the wider economy.

Scurrah says approximately 70 percent of visitors to Fiji travel on Fiji Airways, and reducing flights would affect businesses and jobs that depend on tourism.

He says this is why the airline approached the Government for financial support to maintain its flight operations.

Scurrah explains that the Government's $200 million loan guarantee is not a direct cash payment to Fiji Airways, but provides security for borrowing from financial institutions.

He also reveals that the new 5 percent tourism tax is expected to generate approximately $48 million for the airline this year.

Scurrah says the revenue will help offset some of the additional fuel costs, although Fiji Airways will still have to absorb most of the increase.

He says the airline has developed a five-year plan to return to sustainable profitability and is reviewing its operating costs, investments and business structure.

Scurrah adds that Fiji Airways is also strengthening its fuel hedging programme to better manage future fuel price fluctuations.

Despite the financial challenges, he says the airline remains committed to maintaining flights and supporting Fiji's tourism industry.

Scurrah stresses that the decisions being made now are aimed at ensuring Fiji Airways remains financially strong and sustainable in the years ahead.

item.title: Granddaughter of prominent Lautoka resident set to make history in NZ politics
item.description: Qiulae Wong, the granddaughter of prominent Lautoka resident Eddie Wong, is on track to lead New Zealand's Opportunity Party into Parliament for the first time following a strong showing in Saturday's general election. In the 1940s, Qiulae Wong's grandfather, Eddie Wong established Lukbo as a range of beverages manufactured by his company, Eddie Hin Limited in Lautoka.
item.content:encoded:
Qiulae Wong, the granddaughter of prominent Lautoka resident Eddie Wong, is on track to lead New Zealand's Opportunity Party into Parliament for the first time following a strong showing in Saturday's general election.

In the 1940s, Qiulae Wong's grandfather, Eddie Wong established Lukbo as a range of beverages manufactured by his company, Eddie Hin Limited in Lautoka.

For several decades, Eddie Hin Limited was a leading distributor, manufacturer, and retailer of food and beverages in Fiji, until Eddie's untimely passing in 1992.

As Mayor of Lautoka City, Eddie was a strong advocate for improving outcomes for the local community and played a key role in supporting the settlement of many Chinese migrant families in Fiji.

He also served as a Senator in the Fijian Government and was awarded a Member of the British Empire (MBE) in 1970 in recognition of his service.

Qiulae Wong who leads the Opportunity Party, has told supporters that the party is set to make history after nearly a decade of campaigning for New Zealand parliamentary representation.

With nearly 50 percent of votes counted on election night, the party had secured more than five percent of the votes counted at that stage, putting it on course to cross the threshold required to enter Parliament.

Early results indicated that the Opportunity Party could secure six to seven seats, potentially positioning it to play an important role in determining who forms New Zealand's next government.

Addressing supporters, Wong welcomed the result and thanked the party's candidates, volunteers and supporters for their commitment over the years.

She says voters have chosen unity over division and demonstrated their desire for change in New Zealand politics.

Wong says the result means a great deal to everyone who has worked towards the party's goal of securing representation in Parliament.

She stresses that while the party's breakthrough may appear to have happened overnight, it is the result of nearly a decade of hard work.

The projected result also carries a special connection to Fiji through Wong's family ties to Lautoka.

The final election results are yet to be confirmed.
